name: Tranexamic acid
lead: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic drug first used to control bleeding. In dermatology it has become a popular option for melasma and stubborn hyperpigmentation, applied topically, injected in clinics or taken by mouth.

The cosmetic use of oral tranexamic acid is off-label and prescription-only, while topical products are sold over the counter in many places. Studies show meaningful improvement in melasma but with heterogeneous designs and recurrence after stopping.

paras: It blocks plasmin formation, and in skin this appears to reduce plasmin-driven stimulation of melanocytes and related inflammatory and vascular signalling, decreasing melanin production and the vascular component of melasma.

Topical use is usually well tolerated, with mild irritation. Oral tranexamic acid carries a risk of blood clots and is unsuitable for people with a history of thromboembolism or those on estrogen-containing contraception; gastrointestinal upset and menstrual changes are possible. Oral use requires medical screening and supervision.
